# Generate collision-resistant short codes

Every shortened link needs a compact, URL-safe code that is unlikely to collide and
hard to enumerate. This ticket delivers the codec that mints and validates those codes.

## Design

- Draw 40 bits from a cryptographically secure source.
- Encode with a URL-safe base62 alphabet (no padding, no ambiguous glyphs).
- Reject codes that fail the `^[0-9A-Za-z]{7}$` shape at the boundary.

## Alphabet trade-offs

| Alphabet | Code length | Ambiguity        |
| -------- | ----------- | ---------------- |
| base16   | 10 chars    | none, but long   |
| base62   | 7 chars     | `0/O`, `1/l`[^amb] |
| base58   | 7 chars     | ambiguous removed |

[^amb]: base62 keeps look-alike characters; we accept that for MVP because codes are
    copied, not transcribed. base58 is a v2 follow-up if support tickets say otherwise.

## Reference

```python
from snip.codec import mint, is_valid

code = mint()            # -> "a7Kd93Q"
assert is_valid(code)
```
